ai.title: This featherweight, flying robot carries its own sensors and computers

" Over the past decade, MIT researchers have developed aerial microrobots with bumblebee-like speed, agility, and durability, for tasks like precision agriculture or search-and-rescue. But these featherweight microrobots couldn’t carry the electronics needed for navigation, forcing them to remain connected to a motion-capture system in the lab. Now, the researchers have designed a flapping-wing microrobot with onboard sensors and computation, which can follow a complex trajectory and land precisely on a sunflower outside the lab’s motion capture environment. While the robot is still connected to an offboard power source, this demonstration highlights the potential of aerial microrobots to be used for precision agriculture in the future.

sec.brief: Norwegian Gas Giant Equinor Says It's Under Cyberattack. S. S. 2), in OpenJDK’s Base64 decoder. OpenJDK is the world’s most common Java runtime. OpenJDK (Open Java Development Kit) is the open-source implementation of the Java platform. It provides the tools and components needed to develop and run Java applications, including the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), libraries and development tools. It is widely used in enterprise systems, servers and cloud environments. Base64 shows up everywhere: authentication, file uploads, network messages. To decode it fast, OpenJDK uses special x86-64 instructions that process many bytes at once, and the bug lives in that hand-written machine code. A single malformed string triggers it: 64 “A” characters followed by one equals sign, or 128 on older OpenJDK 17.
